```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

```{r load-package}
library(mixeff)
```

`mixeff` fits linear and generalized linear mixed models in R using
the `mixeff-rs` Rust engine. If you use `lme4`, the formula syntax and
functions such as `fixef()`, `ranef()`, `VarCorr()`, `predict()`, and
`summary()` will be familiar. Supported models are listed by
`supported_models()`; differences in arguments and output are described
in `vignette("lme4-migration")`.

The fitted object stores the model specification, convergence diagnostics,
and the method used for each inference result. You can inspect a singular
fit, find out which tests are available, and save the results for later
use. This vignette demonstrates those steps on a small repeated-measures
dataset, then explains model support and the requirements for restoring
a saved fit.

Tests compare `mixeff` with `lme4` on the datasets shipped with the
package, using documented numerical tolerances. The
[benchmarking article](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mixeff/articles/benchmarking.html)
reports timing comparisons and simulation results, with the package
versions and model designs used in each study.

## The dataset

We simulate 10 daily reaction-time measurements for each of 18 subjects.
The subject intercepts and slopes are nearly perfectly correlated by
construction. This example produces a singular fit in both `lme4` and
`mixeff`.

```{r make-data}
set.seed(3)
n_subj <- 18L
days   <- 0:9
b0     <- rnorm(n_subj, sd = 30)
b1     <- 0.5 * b0 / 30 * 10 + rnorm(n_subj, sd = 0.5)

sleep_like <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_subj), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    subj = factor(i),
    days = days,
    rt   = 250 + b0[i] + (10 + b1[i]) * days +
           rnorm(length(days), sd = 20)
  )
}))

head(sleep_like, 4)
```

## Fitting a model

The formula below estimates a population slope for `days` and allows
each subject to have a different intercept and slope.

```{r fit-model}
fit <- lmm(
  rt ~ days + (1 + days | subj),
  sleep_like,
  control = mm_control(verbose = -1)
)
fit
```

```{r familiar-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(fit, "mm_lmm"))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(fixef(fit))))
stopifnot(length(fitted(fit)) == nrow(sleep_like))
```

`fixef()`, `ranef()`, `VarCorr()`, `predict()`, `simulate()`, `anova()`, and
`summary()` all work on this fit; `vignette("lme4-migration")` lists where
their output differs from lme4's.

## Singular fits

In this example, the fitted random-effect covariance has reduced rank.
Use `fit_status()` and `is_singular()` to inspect the result:

```{r singular-status}
fit_status(fit)
is_singular(fit)
```

```{r singular-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(fit_status(fit), "converged_reduced_rank"))
stopifnot(isTRUE(is_singular(fit)))
```

`diagnostics()` gives more detail, and `changes()` compares the requested
model with its effective specification and fitted covariance. See
`vignette("convergence", package = "mixeff")` for the meaning of each
status and the consequences for inference.

## Available inference methods

`inference_options()` lists the methods available for a fitted model,
explains any restrictions, and gives the function call for each method.
The status and reason codes are defined in the
[inference-method glossary](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mixeff/articles/inference-method-glossary.html).

```{r inference-options}
opt <- inference_options(fit, "days", nsim = 200)
opt$table[, c("method", "expected_status",
              "expected_reliability_reason", "current")]
```

```{r options-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(opt, "mm_inference_options"))
stopifnot(any(opt$table$expected_status == "available"))
stopifnot(any(opt$table$expected_status != "available"))
```

For this singular fit, `mixeff` withholds Satterthwaite and Kenward–Roger
tests. Parametric bootstrap tests remain available. The inference vignette
explains these restrictions and demonstrates the alternatives:
`vignette("inference", package = "mixeff")`.

An inference result includes its method and status. If a requested
quantity is unavailable, the function returns a reason code with the
result or raises a typed error.

## Supported models

`supported_models()` reads the package's support registry
(`inst/support/model-support.json`). Tests check that the registry,
fitting code, and documentation agree.

```{r supported-envelope}
sm <- supported_models()
knitr::kable(sm$glmm_families[, c("family", "links", "estimators")],
             caption = "GLMM family/link/estimator cells, from the registry.")
knitr::kable(sm$features[, c("feature", "lmm", "glmm")],
             caption = "Feature support, from the registry.")
```

```{r envelope-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(sm, "mm_model_support"))
stopifnot(nrow(sm$glmm_families) >= 4L, nrow(sm$features) >= 5L)
stopifnot(length(sm$non_goals) >= 1L, all(nzchar(sm$non_goals)))
```

Explicit non-goals, from the same registry:
`r paste(sm$non_goals, collapse = "; ")`.

For the full tables, including notes on individual features, see
`vignette("lme4-migration", package = "mixeff")`. When comparing results
with lme4, keep two qualifications in mind:

- Estimates are not bit-for-bit identical to `lme4`; the criterion is
  agreement within documented tolerances on the parity
  datasets shipped with the package. Where results are *expected* to
  differ, the differences are classified in
  `inst/extdata/expected-mismatches.json`, with tolerances enforced
  by the test suite.
- Generalized fits have estimator-specific inference methods;
  see `vignette("glmm", package = "mixeff")` for the estimators and
  `vignette("inference", package = "mixeff")` for the inference
  routes.

## Saving and restoring a fit

Save a fit with `saveRDS()` and reload it with `readRDS()`. The stored
coefficients and diagnostics remain available after reloading:

```{r round-trip}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(fit, path)
restored_fit <- revive(readRDS(path))

identical(fixef(restored_fit),             fixef(fit))
identical(changes(restored_fit)$table,     changes(fit)$table)
identical(diagnostics(restored_fit)$table, diagnostics(fit)$table)
```

```{r round-trip-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(fixef(restored_fit), fixef(fit)))
stopifnot(identical(changes(restored_fit)$table, changes(fit)$table))
stopifnot(identical(diagnostics(restored_fit)$table, diagnostics(fit)$table))
```

### Operations on a restored fit

Stored coefficients, fitted values, variance components, and audit
records are available after `readRDS()` without a live Rust handle.
The checks above compare these stored values before and after saving.

New LMM contrasts and term tests, conditional random-effect variances,
engine-backed prediction, and prediction uncertainty reuse a live native
handle. After serialization, native queries restore the recorded fitted
state without running an optimizer. `revive()` resets the R cache and clears
a dead handle; restoration rebuilds matrix factors at the saved parameters.
Derivative calculations required by an inference method may still take time.

Restoration requires a matching engine source and build configuration. A
fit without a live handle and without a compatible snapshot keeps its stored
extractors but refuses native queries that require restoration.
Keep the package and engine build with the saved fit when reproducing an
analysis. Explicit refitting, bootstrap, profile intervals and convergence
verification still perform the optimization those operations request.

```{r persist-data, include = FALSE}
set.seed(42)
n_clinic <- 12L
n_per_clinic <- 6L
clinic <- factor(rep(seq_len(n_clinic), each = n_per_clinic))
week <- rep(0:(n_per_clinic - 1L), n_clinic)
treatment <- factor(
  rep(rep(c("usual", "coached"), each = n_per_clinic), length.out = length(week)),
  levels = c("usual", "coached")
)
clinic_shift <- rnorm(n_clinic, sd = 0.45)
score <- 7.2 - 0.28 * week - 0.55 * (treatment == "coached") +
  clinic_shift[as.integer(clinic)] + rnorm(length(week), sd = 0.35)
clinic_visits <- data.frame(score, week, treatment, clinic)
```

```{r persist-fit}
fit2 <- lmm(
  score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic),
  clinic_visits,
  control = mm_control(verbose = -1)
)

path2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(fit2, path2)

restored <- readRDS(path2)
restored <- revive(restored)
```

`revive()` resets the object's process-local cache. You can call it after
`readRDS()`, but the extractors and
inference functions shown below also work on the plain `readRDS()`
result. Stored extractors read durable values; operations requiring a native
model restore the saved state as described above when no live handle remains.

```{r persist-extractors}
fixef(restored)
head(predict(restored))
reporting_table(restored, "fixed_effects")
```

```{r persist-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(fixef(restored), fixef(fit2)))
stopifnot(length(predict(restored)) == nrow(clinic_visits))
stopifnot(identical(reporting_table(restored, "fixed_effects"),
                    reporting_table(fit2, "fixed_effects")))
```

Conditional variances for random effects can also be requested after reload.
The engine restores the saved fit without optimization. With `condVar = TRUE`,
each grouping table in this example carries a finite `postVar` array.

```{r persist-condvar}
re <- ranef(restored, condVar = TRUE)
attr(re, "mm_unavailable_reason")
dim(attr(re$clinic, "postVar"))
```

```{r condvar-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(is.null(attr(re, "mm_unavailable_reason")))
stopifnot(is.array(attr(re$clinic, "postVar")))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(attr(re$clinic, "postVar"))))
```

For details of `vcov()`, see `vignette("inference", package = "mixeff")`.
Rebuilding design matrices with `model.matrix()` and `getME()` is
demonstrated in `vignette("lmm", package = "mixeff")`.

### Stored records and schemas

The structured JSON artifacts stored in the fitted object are the
source of truth; external pointers such as the Rust handle are
caches. `mm_json_known_schemas()` lists the artifact schemas this
version of the package understands:

```{r schemas}
head(mm_json_known_schemas())
```

```{r schema-checks, include = FALSE}
schemas <- mm_json_known_schemas()
stopifnot(is.data.frame(schemas))
stopifnot(all(c("name", "version") %in% names(schemas)))
stopifnot(nrow(schemas) >= 1L)
```

## Lower-level tools

Most users start with `lmm()`, `glmm()`, `summary()`, `contrast()`,
`test_effect()`, `compare()`, and `reporting_table()`. The
lower-level functions are there when you need them:

- `mm_parse_formula()` checks formula syntax and returns the
  canonical spelling (demonstrated in
  `vignette("lmm", package = "mixeff")`).
- `compile_model()` builds a pre-fit model specification;
  `explain_model()` translates it into named forms and plain-language
  scopes (also in `vignette("lmm", package = "mixeff")`).
- `diagnostics()` and `changes()` expose model-state checks.
- `mm_json_known_schemas()` lists the structured artifact schemas
  understood by this version of the package.
